sources.entry: pelican - Static site generator that supports Markdown and reST syntax.

summary.one_liner: Pelican is a Python static site generator that turns Markdown, reStructuredText, and HTML source files into a static website.
summary.what_it_does: Pelican reads content written in Markdown, reStructuredText, or HTML and generates a complete static site of HTML, CSS, and JS from it. It supports chronological content such as articles and blog posts as well as standalone static pages. Site appearance is controlled by themes built from Jinja2 templates. It can produce Atom and RSS feeds, publish articles in multiple languages, and highlight code with Pygments. The README also says it can import existing content from WordPress, Dotclear, or RSS feeds, and that content caching and selective output writing speed up rebuilds. A command-line tool performs the generation, and the README notes it works with version control and web hooks.
use_cases: build a personal blog without a database
publish a static documentation or content website
convert WordPress or Dotclear posts to static pages
write blog posts in Markdown and generate HTML
generate Atom or RSS feeds for a site
host a multilingual website as static files
notable: Accepts Markdown, reStructuredText, and HTML source files
Imports content from WordPress, Dotclear, or RSS feeds
Output is fully static and can be served from any web server or host
Extensible through a plugin ecosystem (Pelican Plugins)
Content caching and selective output writing for faster rebuilds
caveats: The README does not state installation or run commands, so setup details must be taken from the documentation
Generates static output only, so it has no built-in server-side or dynamic features
keywords: build static site from text files
make a blog without a database
publish blog posts from markdown files
